title: top-up: in-guest memory guard for the agent run
definition: Review that the in-guest memory guard acts only on a Linux memory reading below its floor (3% of total, never under 256 MiB), that it SIGKILLs only the largest process in the agent run's own tree (never the agent itself, the worker's own pid, or a process outside the tree), that a reading without byte counts or an unknown reading never triggers it, and that every guard kill, and every kill that fails, is logged rather than swallowed.
